title: Structures, Unions and Enums
goal: Struct, nested struct, array of structs, pointer/arrow, union, enum, typedef, padding aur self-referential struct.
definition: Structure alag-alag types ke members ko ek naam ke neeche group karta hai; union same memory ko alag types se interpret karta hai; enum named integer constants deta hai.
explain: struct Student { int roll; char name[32]; float marks; }; definition hai; struct Student s; object. Member access dot se, pointer se arrow (->).
Struct assignment value copy karti hai (deep copy nahi — pointer members shared rehte hain). Function me by value copy hoti hai; bade struct pointer se bhejo.
Union ke saare members same memory share karte hain — ek waqt me ek valid. Size sabse bade member ke barabar (plus alignment).
Padding alignment ke liye aati hai; sizeof struct members ke sum se bada ho sakta hai. Members ko bade se chhote order karne se padding kam hoti hai.
Self-referential struct (struct Node { struct Node *next; }) linked list ka base hai.
analogy: Struct ek form hai jisme alag-alag fields ek saath rakhe jaate hain; union ek hi dabba hai jisme alag-alag label laga sakte ho par ek waqt me ek hi saaman.
why: Real data (student, employee, node) struct me model hota hai; enums states/flags readable banate hain; linked lists aur trees self-referential structs hain.

syntax.code:
typedef enum { RED, GREEN = 5, BLUE } Color;
typedef union { int i; float f; unsigned char bytes[4]; } Value;
syntax.note: enum values auto-increment; union members overlap.

topics.title: Struct basics
topics.body: Declaration, initialization (designated .marks = 91.5 bhi), member access, assignment copy, array of structs, nested struct.

topics.title: Pointers aur functions
topics.body: p->member == (*p).member. Struct by value bhejne par copy hoti hai; modify karne ke liye pointer. Struct return karna allowed hai.

topics.title: Union, enum, typedef
topics.body: Union memory bachata hai par active member track karna padta hai (tagged union). Enum switch ke saath readable. typedef naam chhota karta hai.

topics.title: Padding, alignment, bit-fields
topics.body: sizeof(struct {char c; int i;}) usually 8, 5 nahi. bit-fields (unsigned flags:3) space bachate hain par layout implementation-defined. Self-referential struct linked structures ke liye.

examples.title: Student struct
lines: typedef ne struct ka naam Student kar diya.
p->name pointer ke through member hai.

examples.title: Union aur enum
lines: Enum active type track karta hai.
Union dono values ko same memory me rakhta hai.
sizeof tagged union ~8 bytes (tag + largest member/alignment).

visual.title: struct { char c; int i; } layout
rows: Members reorder: int i; char c; -> size 8 hi, par cache behtar

mistakes.why: Dot object ke liye, arrow pointer ke liye.

mistakes.wrong: union me ek member likh kar doosra padhna
mistakes.right: tag se active member track karo
mistakes.why: Type punning implementation-defined/UB ho sakta hai.

mistakes.right: member-wise ya memcmp (padding ke saath careful)
mistakes.why: C me struct equality operator nahi hai.

debug.brief: sizeof(Student) 40 aa raha hai 36 ki jagah. Reason batao.
hints: Alignment ke liye gaps aate hain.
33 ke baad int 4-byte aligned hota hai.
debug.fix: Members ko bade se chhote order karo ya padding accept karo; sizeof implementation-defined hai.

interview.a: CPU aligned access fast karta hai; compiler members ko unke alignment par rakhta hai, beech me gaps chhodta hai. sizeof isliye sum se bada hota hai.
interview.followUp: Padding kam kaise? — members ko size ke descending order me rakho.

interview.q: Struct by value pass karna kab bura?
interview.a: Bade struct ki copy expensive hoti hai aur function original modify nahi kar sakta. const pointer bhejo.
interview.followUp: Return by value? — compiler often optimize karta hai (RVO).
